paper.title: Flexible and Efficient Contextual Bandits with Heterogeneous Treatment Effect Oracles

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic contextual bandit with treatment effect model class (R-loss oracle, possibly misspecified)
unmapped: Learner has a treatment-effect model class G and an R-loss oracle with known excess-risk estimation rate xi(n, zeta) (Assumption 1)
Misspecification measured by R-loss average misspecification B = max_p min_{g in G} E_p(g), unknown to the learner
settings.definition_quote: At each round $t$, nature randomly samples a context-reward pair $(x_t, r_t)$ from a fixed but unknown probability distribution $D$ over the joint space of contexts and reward vectors $\calX\times[0,1]^K$. The learner observes $x_t$, chooses an action $a_t\in\calA$, and receives the reward $r_t(a_t)\in[0,1]$ for the chosen action.

algorithms.name: HTE-IGW (Heterogeneous Treatment Effect Inverse Gap Weighting)

symbols.Xi_sum: sum_{t=tau_1+1}^T sqrt(xi(tau_{m(t)-1}-tau_{m(t)-2}, delta'/m(t)^2)), where xi is the R-loss oracle estimation rate and m(t) the epoch of round t
symbols.B_mis: R-loss average misspecification B = max_p min_{g in G} E_p(g)

conditions: R-loss oracle satisfies Assumption 1 (excess risk <= xi(n,zeta) + C_0 B w.p. 1-zeta)
misspecification test satisfies Assumptions 2 and 3 (e.g. safety check of Krishnamurthy et al. 2021)

source.label: thm:main-theorem
source.quote: Suppose the $R$-loss oracle satisfies Assumption \ref{ass:main-assumption}. Then, with probability at least $1-\delta$, $\HIGW$ attains the following regret guarantee: \text{Reg}(T)\leq\ordO\Bigg(\sum_{t=\tau_1+1}^{T}\sqrt{K\xi\left(\tau_{m(t)-1}-\tau_{m(t)-2},\frac{\delta'}{m(t)^2}\right)} +\sqrt{KB}T\Bigg).

results.notes: Regret is realized regret sum_t r_t(pi*(x_t)) - r_t(a_t) bounded w.p. 1-delta. With tau_m = 2^m the text states Reg(T) <= O(sqrt(K xi(T, delta'/log T)) T + sqrt(KB) T). B is not known to the learner. Proof relies on assumed safety-check properties.

symbols.B_mis: R-loss average misspecification B = max_p min_{g in G} E_p(g)

conditions: linear treatment effect class G = {(x,a) -> <theta, x_a> : ||theta||_2 <= 1}, ||x_a||_2 <= 1
R-loss oracle (R-learner) with least-squares excess risk rates as in Simchi-Levi and Xu (2021)

source.quote: Consider the following class of linear treatment effects \calG=\{g:(x,a)\mapsto \langle\theta, x_a\rangle\mid\theta\in\R^d,||\theta||_2\le1\} ... In particular, we have $\text{Reg}(T)\le\calO(\sqrt{KT(d+\log T)} + \sqrt{KB}T)$.

results.notes: Stated in an Example environment, not a theorem; dependence on delta suppressed. Specialization of Theorem 1 to linear treatment effects.
